## Key Requirements

Starting May 5, 2025, Microsoft requires DMARC, SPF & DKIM for bulk emails to Outlook. These rules apply to anyone sending over 5,000 emails per day to Microsoft consumer services such as Outlook.com, Hotmail.com, and Live.com.

A valid DMARC policy is required, with a minimum policy of p=none that must align with SPF or DKIM—ideally both.

## Authentication Methods

The three authentication requirements are:

## What is Spintax?

Spintax (short for "spinning syntax") is a simple text format that lets you define multiple variations of a word or phrase within a single message template. Spintax tools turn one email template into dozens or hundreds of unique variations using curly-brace syntax: {Hi|Hello|Hey}.

## The Deliverability Problem it Solves

Spintax solves the single biggest deliverability killer in cold email: duplicate content. When you send the exact same email body to 200, 500, or 1,000 recipients through the same mailbox or domain, Gmail and Outlook's spam filters notice. They compare message fingerprints across sends, and when they see identical content going to multiple recipients from the same sender, they classify it as bulk mail.

## Risk Detection & How Spintax Works

Email service providers (ESPs) and spam filters compare message content across recipients. When they detect identical text being sent in volume, deliverability suffers. Spam filters cannot match your emails to a bulk send pattern because there is no single pattern to match. Your 1,000-prospect campaign looks like 1,000 individual sends, because the text actually is different in each one.

## 2026 Insights on Effectiveness

According to Hunter.io's 2026 State of Cold Email report, emails with at least two personalizations achieve a 5.6% reply rate compared to 3.6% for emails with zero personalization, a 56% improvement. However, word-level spintax barely moves deliverability. Sentence-level and paragraph-level spintax with 6-10 meaningful variations is where the lift actually comes from.

## Important Limitations

Spintax is a supporting measure, not a complete solution. Deliverability depends on a lot more than content variation. Fix deliverability issues at the domain level first — SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and proper warm-up.

# Cold Email Engine — Phase 3 Research & Build Spec

Research compiled **2026-08-11**. Cold email is a fast-moving space (ISP rules + regulation change quarterly), so every claim below is dated and cited. Treat anything older than ~12 months as "verify before relying on it."

> **TL;DR for the owner:** The single most important 2026 change is that **open rate is no longer a real metric** and **inbox access is now gated by mandatory authentication, not by content**. Apple Mail Privacy Protection (MPP) auto-opens ~50%+ of email, so open rate is inflated noise; meanwhile Google/Yahoo (Feb 2024) and Microsoft (May 2025) will *reject* mail that isn't SPF+DKIM+DMARC authenticated with one-click unsubscribe and a spam-complaint rate under 0.3%. Phase 3 must be built around **reply rate, bounce rate, complaint rate, and inbox-placement** — not opens — and around **health-monitored multi-inbox rotation with auto-pause**, because a single burned domain now poisons all recipients on it.

---

## 1) Active open-source platforms (2026)

Important framing: there is **no fully-featured OSS clone of Instantly/Smartlead** that includes a real shared warmup network — the network effect (tens of thousands of vetted, engaged mailboxes) is the moat those SaaS products actually sell, and it can't be self-hosted alone. OSS covers the *sending/campaign/MTA* layer well and the *warmup* layer poorly. Categorize as: (A) sending MTAs, (B) campaign/marketing platforms, (C) cold-email/warmup-specific tools.

### A. Sending MTAs (the outbound engine)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Postal** | App-oriented mail platform: SMTP send, inbound routing, webhooks, IP pools, multi-tenant orgs, DKIM/SPF/Return-Path. Docker/K8s, OIDC SSO, Prometheus metrics. Actively maintained. | Ruby on Rails, MySQL/MariaDB, RabbitMQ | MIT | Yes | Open (1x1 pixel), click (link rewrite), delivery/bounce via webhooks, Prometheus |

| **Mailcow / Mailu / Stalwart** | Full mailbox servers (Postfix/Dovecot etc.), not cold-email tools. Good for *hosting the actual mailboxes/IMAP* an outreach tool sends through. Mailcow = polished SMB UI; Stalwart = low-resource Rust; Mailu = minimal/K8s. | Various | Various (mostly permissive/GPL) | Yes | Server-level, not campaign-level |

### B. Campaign / email-marketing platforms (broadcast, not cold-outreach-native)

| Tool | Stack | License | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **listmonk** | Go + Postgres | AGPLv3 | Fast, simple, high-performance lists/campaigns; needs external SMTP relay (SES/Mailgun). Opens/clicks/bounces. |
| **Mautic** | PHP/Symfony | GPLv3 | Deepest OSS marketing automation (segmentation, campaign flows, scoring). Heavier. |

GPLv3 (Mautic, Mailtrain) has no network clause; private SaaS modifications stay private. ### C. Cold-email / warmup-specific OSS (thin, verify before trusting)

- **Warmbly** — the closest thing to an OSS Instantly/Smartlead. The honest 2026 conclusion: **a legitimate, self-hosted, mature OSS warmup *network* does not exist** — you either build a private engagement loop yourself or rent a network.

Sources: [dev.to open-source email warmup guide](https://dev.to/tusharsmtpmaster/open-source-email-warmup-a-complete-guide-5d5b), [github esli351/best-email-tools](https://github.com/esli351/best-email-tools).

**Implication for Nxeon:** Phase 3 is not "adopt an OSS platform." It's "keep the existing Next.js/Prisma app as the control plane, send through customers' own IMAP/SMTP mailboxes (or a Postal/KumoMTA relay), and build warmup + analytics + rotation ourselves." Postal is the best OSS reference for the *events/webhooks/tracking* model; KumoMTA is the reference if we ever run our own IPs.

---

## 2) Email warming — current mechanics (2026)

**Why it still exists:** Gmail and Microsoft tightened filtering; brand-new domains/inboxes are flagged immediately. Warmup builds a history of "normal, trusted" sending — gradually rising volume + positive engagement (opens, replies, marking important, rescuing from spam) — so that by the time a real campaign sends, the provider already trusts the sender. ([omnisend warmup 2026](https://www.omnisend.com/blog/warm-up-email-domain/), [reply.io warm-up 2026](https://reply.io/warm-up-email/))

**Modern ramp schedule (consensus 2026):**
- New inbox starts ~**5–10 emails/day**, ramps to **40–50/day** over **2–4 weeks** (MailReach's default is ~10/day wk1 → 40–50 by wk4). A "fully warmed" inbox tops out around **50–100/day** at **3–5 weeks**. ([mailreach gmail warmup](https://www.mailreach.co/blog/gmail-warmup), [leadhaste timeline](https://leadhaste.com/blog/email-warmup-timeline-and-schedule))
- Pre-warmed inboxes can start higher (Smartlead guidance: ~80/day wk1 → 150–180 by day 30). ([litemail smartlead warmup](https://litemail.ai/blog/email-warmup-smartlead-best-tool-2026))
- **AI/adaptive ramp** is now standard: Smartlead/MailReach adjust ramp speed in real time off a live "health score" instead of a fixed daily increment. MailReach cites a network of 30,000+ Google Workspace / M365 accounts + a "Co-Pilot" that reads deliverability signals. ([maildeck warmup tools 2026](https://maildeck.co/blog/best-email-warm-up-tools-2026/))

**Warmup activities the networks simulate:** send between pool inboxes, auto-open, auto-reply, mark-as-important/star, and **rescue from spam → move to inbox** (the strongest signal). Seed inboxes across Gmail/M365/Yahoo. ([smartlead warm-up guide](https://www.smartlead.ai/blog/email-warm-up-guide))

**The 2026 debate — does artificial warmup still help, or now hurt?** This is genuinely contested and Phase 3 must be honest about it:
- **Against:** most warmup tools generate *artificial* opens/clicks between simulated inboxes — literally trying to manipulate the spam filters whose job is to protect real users. Recent Gmail/Yahoo updates that reward *long-term domain reputation and real authentication* are increasingly good at detecting these synthetic patterns, and **when detected can actively damage deliverability**. ([omnisend 2026](https://www.omnisend.com/blog/warm-up-email-domain/), [prospeo deliverability](https://prospeo.io/s/email-deliverability-best-practices))
- **For (quality networks):** Instantly's 2026 Cold Email Benchmark Report claims *private, vetted* networks deliver 20–30% higher post-warmup inbox placement than public pools, because they exclude spam traps and reputation-damaged domains before entry. ([leadhaste high-volume warmup](https://leadhaste.com/blog/email-warmup-for-high-volume-sending))
- **Emerging best practice:** favor **real engagement** — genuine replies from a small seed audience, low-and-slow real sends to engaged recipients, and steady authenticated volume — over synthetic pool traffic. The safest posture is warmup that produces *replies and spam-recovery on a vetted pool*, not mass auto-opens.

---

## 3) Deliverability tactics 2026

**Isolate the sending domain (universal in 2026).** Never cold-send from the primary brand domain — at volume it now *burns* the primary. Buy separate lookalike domains (e.g. `try-brand.com`, `getbrand.co`) and send from a **subdomain** (`mail.` / `outreach.`) so any reputation damage is quarantined off the root. ([growleads subdomain](https://growleads.io/blog/subdomain-for-cold-email-protect-main-domain/), [unifygtm cold email 2026](https://www.unifygtm.com/explore/cold-email-2026-domain-setup-deliverability-sequences))

**Domain + inbox rotation (the core scaling primitive):**
- Serious teams run **3–5 domains**, each with **4–6 inboxes**, rotating daily. ([firstsales domain rotation](https://firstsales.io/blog/email-domain-rotation/), [litemail inbox rotation](https://litemail.ai/blog/cold-email-agency-inbox-rotation-best-practices-2026))
- **Per-inbox daily cap: 20–40** for a warmed inbox (newer inboxes 10–15), i.e. **~100–250/domain/day** across 3–5 inboxes. Space sends **90–120s apart** across a sending window — 40 rapid sends in an hour reads as bot behavior. ([ozigi caps](https://ozigi.app/blog/how-many-cold-emails-per-day-without-spam))

**Authentication (mandatory — see §5):** SPF + DKIM + DMARC on every sending domain, warmed 2–4 weeks before volume.

**Custom tracking domain:** always use your own tracking subdomain (e.g. `t.mail-brand.com`) instead of the tool's shared one; shared tracking domains are widely blocklisted and tank placement. Only enable open tracking behind a custom domain (and see §4 on why opens barely matter now). ([mailflowauthority infra](https://mailflowauthority.com/cold-email/cold-email-infrastructure-complete-guide))

**Content variation / spintax:** the #1 content-level deliverability killer is **duplicate content** — identical bodies to many recipients from one domain get fingerprinted as bulk. Spintax (`{Hi|Hello|Hey}`) makes each send unique. **Nuance:** word-level spintax "barely moves deliverability"; **sentence/paragraph-level variation with 6–10 meaningful variants** is where the lift is. Personalization matters more: emails with ≥2 personalizations get 5.6% reply vs 3.6% with none (Hunter.io 2026 State of Cold Email). ([smartlead spintax](https://www.smartlead.ai/blog/what-is-spintax), [mailreach spintax](https://www.mailreach.co/blog/spintax-cold-email))

**Inbox-placement / seed testing:** don't trust "delivered" — test where mail actually lands.
- **GlockApps** — ~$59/mo, 70+ seed addresses (Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo/corporate + regional EU/APAC), reports inbox vs spam vs Promotions/Updates vs missing, plus DMARC analytics + blocklist monitoring + content analysis. ([mailflowauthority glockapps](https://mailflowauthority.com/esp-reviews/glockapps-review))
- **MailReach spam test** — 30+ real Google Workspace/M365/Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo mailboxes; inbox/spam/promotions breakdown. ([mailreach spam test tools](https://www.mailreach.co/blog/email-spam-test-tools))

**List verification (pre-send, non-negotiable for bounce control):** ZeroBounce / NeverBounce / Bouncer / MillionVerifier all sit at **97–99% accuracy**. The real differentiator is **catch-all handling** (15–28% of B2B domains are catch-all where *no* tool can confirm the mailbox); Bouncer claims ~87% catch-all detection vs 40–60% for others. Verify every list immediately before send, not at import (addresses decay). ([instantly verification benchmark 2026](https://instantly.ai/blog/2026-email-verification-benchmark-accuracy-scores-for-8-top-tools/), [usebouncer best tools](https://www.usebouncer.com/best-email-verification-tools/))

**Bounce & complaint handling:** hard bounce → suppress permanently, never retry; soft bounce → limited retry then suppress; complaint (FBL/List-Unsubscribe) → suppress + investigate targeting (see §4 thresholds).

**BIMI:** requires DMARC at **enforcement** (p=quarantine pct=100 or p=reject) + a logo cert (VMC ≈ $1,500/yr needs a trademark and unlocks Gmail's blue check; CMC is cheaper, no Gmail check, shows logo in Yahoo/Apple). **Verdict for cold email: skip it.** Outlook ignores BIMI (and most B2B is on M365), cold subdomains have no prior brand association, and the measured lift is only 2–6% and only on Gmail-web/Apple/Yahoo. Reserve BIMI for the *warm* brand domain, not outreach. ([redsift BIMI 2026](https://redsift.com/guides/bimi-in-2026-verified-logos-cmcs-and-the-fastest-path-to-inbox-display), [puzzleinbox BIMI cold email](https://puzzleinbox.com/blog/bimi-cold-email-setup-worth-it-2026))

## 4) Analytics that actually matter now

**Metric definitions (2026):**
- **Delivery rate** = accepted by receiving server ÷ sent. High delivery ≠ inbox; it only means "not bounced/rejected." Do not confuse with placement.
- **Inbox-placement rate** = of delivered mail, % landing in the primary inbox (vs spam/Promotions/missing). Measured via seed tests (§3), *not* from your own send logs. **Good ≥90%, best-in-class ≥95%.** ([amplemarket 2026 benchmarks](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/cold-email-benchmarks))
- **Open rate** = pixel loads ÷ delivered. **Largely broken — see below.**
- **Click rate** = unique clickers ÷ delivered. More reliable than opens but distorted by security scanners/link-preview bots that auto-click.
- **Bounce rate** = bounces ÷ sent. **Hard bounce** = permanent (bad/nonexistent address) → suppress forever. **Soft bounce** = temporary (mailbox full, greylisting, size).
- **Spam-complaint rate** = complaints ÷ delivered (via Postmaster/FBL).
- **Unsubscribe rate** = unsubs ÷ delivered.
- **Reply rate** and **positive-reply rate** = replies (and positive/interested replies) ÷ delivered. **The KPI that matters most in 2026.**

**Open tracking is unreliable — be honest in the UI.** Apple Mail Privacy Protection (since 2021, escalated through iOS 18) **pre-loads all remote content including tracking pixels on Apple's servers**, so emails register as "opened" even when unread. Apple Mail is ~51% of the global email-client market and **>55% of all global opens now come from Apple/MPP devices** — meaning the majority of "opens" are machine-generated. Corporate security scanners (Proofpoint/Mimecast/Defender) also pre-fetch pixels *and* links. **Net: open rate is inflated, non-comparable, and unsafe as an optimization target or a health signal.** ([sender.net MPP 2026 guide](https://www.sender.net/blog/apple-mail-privacy-protection/), [hustlermarketing 3 metrics replacing open rate](https://www.hustlermarketing.com/blog/3-email-metrics-that-are-replacing-open-rate-in-2026/), [instantly open-tracking accuracy](https://instantly.ai/blog/email-open-tracking-how-it-works-accuracy-rates-and-why-your-open-metrics-may-be-wrong/))

**What leaders optimize instead (MPP-proof signals):**
1. **Reply rate / positive-reply rate** — replies require human intent; mailbox providers treat replies as a strong positive trust signal. This is the primary campaign KPI.
2. **Click rate** — MPP-resistant (MPP proxies pixels, not user clicks), though filter clicking distorts it.
3. **Complaint rate + bounce rate + unsubscribe rate** — combined into a "disaffection/disengagement" index; the clearest early warning of a burning domain.
4. **Inbox-placement rate** from seed tests — the ground truth for "are we even in the inbox."

**Benchmarks (2026, deliverability-managed vs raw):**
| Metric | Good | Best-in-class | Danger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inbox placement | ≥90% | ≥95% | <80% |
| Bounce | <3% | <1.5% | >5% → stop & diagnose |
| Reply | 1–5% | 8–10%+ | — |
| Spam complaint | <0.1% | ~0% | 0.3% hard ceiling |
| Open (context only) | 15–25% raw | not a target | ignore |
Source: [amplemarket 2026](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/cold-email-benchmarks).

**"Domain/inbox is burning" thresholds (auto-pause triggers):**
- **Bounce:** <2% safe · 2–5% warning (Postmaster reputation degrading, clean list before continuing) · >5% danger (immediate pause + re-verify). Sustained >2% for 5–7 days suppresses inbox placement for *all* Gmail recipients on that domain, not just the bad addresses. **Recommended auto-pause at ~1.8% per inbox/day** (before the ceiling). ([litemail bounce thresholds](https://litemail.ai/blog/cold-email-inbox-bounce-rate-thresholds-2026))
- **Complaint:** <0.05% safe · 0.05–0.08% warning · **>0.08% pause the whole domain and investigate targeting** (Google effectively treats ~0.1%+ as a problem; 0.3% is the hard mandate ceiling). Complaint spikes = wrong ICP or deceptive copy. ([amplemarket](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/cold-email-benchmarks), [litemail health metrics](https://litemail.ai/blog/cold-email-inbox-health-metrics-2026))

## 5) CURRENT regulation + ISP requirements (the fast-changing part) — what's mandatory NOW

This is what gates the inbox *at all* in 2026. Non-compliant senders see **22–34% of mail routed to spam vs 89% inbox placement for compliant senders** — a 3–7x penalty. ([mailover 2026 guide](https://mailover.ai/blog/bulk-sender-requirements.html))

**Google + Yahoo — "Yahoogle" (announced Oct 2023, enforced Feb 1 2024), for senders of 5,000+/day to consumer Gmail/Yahoo:**
- **SPF + DKIM** both configured and passing; **at least one aligned** to the From-header domain.
- **DMARC** published, minimum **p=none** with a RUA reporting tag.
- **One-click unsubscribe** per **RFC 8058** (`List-Unsubscribe` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post`), processed **within 2 days**.
- **Spam complaint rate < 0.3%** (hard ceiling) via **Google Postmaster Tools**; operational target **< 0.1%**.
- Valid forward + reverse DNS (FCrDNS) and TLS on transmission.
- **Escalation:** Feb 2024 = temp deferrals (421-4.7.26/.30/.32); **Nov 2025 Gmail escalated to permanent rejection (550-5.7.26)** for unauthenticated mail. Full enforcement across providers in 2026. ([redsift 2026 checklist](https://redsift.com/guides/bulk-email-sender-requirements), [mailgun yahoogle](https://www.mailgun.com/state-of-email-deliverability/chapter/yahoogle-bulk-senders/), [autospf two years on](https://autospf.com/blog/google-yahoo-bulk-sender-mandate-changes-over-two-years/))

**Microsoft / Outlook (enforced May 5 2025), for 5,000+/day to Outlook.com/Hotmail.com/Live.com:**
- **SPF + DKIM + DMARC** all required; DMARC min **p=none**, aligned to SPF or DKIM (ideally both).
- Non-compliant mail was first **junked**, moving toward **rejection**; treat SPF+DKIM+DMARC as mandatory to reach Outlook consumer inboxes. Microsoft doesn't publish the 0.3% number but the same hygiene applies. ([microsoft tech community](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftdefenderforoffice365blog/strengthening-email-ecosystem-outlook%E2%80%99s-new-requirements-for-high%E2%80%90volume-senders/4399730), [mailgun MS requirements](https://www.mailgun.com/blog/deliverability/microsoft-sender-requirements/), [validity MS rules](https://www.validity.com/blog/keeping-the-inbox-safe-microsofts-new-bulk-email-rules-explained/))

> **Cold-email caveat:** the 5,000/day thresholds are *per-provider consumer volume*. A rotation setup sending 20–40/inbox stays under it per inbox — but **compliance is not optional even below 5k**: sub-threshold senders that fail auth or spike complaints still get filtered, and the auth requirements are now the de-facto floor for *any* sender. Build to the strict standard regardless of volume.

**Legislation (status + 2025–2026 changes):**
- **CAN-SPAM (US):** permissive — cold email allowed without prior consent, but requires accurate From/subject, a functional opt-out honored promptly, and a **valid physical postal address** (commonly missed). Penalty raised to **up to $53,088 per email, effective Jan 17 2025**. ([instantly compliance](https://instantly.ai/blog/b2b-email-list-compliance-gdpr-canspam/), [growleads is cold email legal 2026](https://growleads.io/blog/is-cold-email-legal-gdpr-can-spam-2026/))
- **GDPR (EU/UK):** B2B cold email allowed under **legitimate interest** (no explicit consent) *only* with a documented Legitimate Interest Assessment, business (not personal) addresses, role-relevant messaging, disclosure of data source, and easy opt-out. Fines up to **€20M / 4% global revenue**. **New:** France's **CNIL rules effective Aug 2026 require explicit opt-in for all B2C prospecting** (email/phone/SMS) — watch for other member states following. ([outreachbloom compliance 2026](https://outreachbloom.com/cold-email-compliance), [inboxkit compliance](https://www.inboxkit.com/learn/cold-email-compliance-gdpr-can-spam))
- **CASL (Canada):** strictest — **consent required before the first send** (express or implied via an existing business relationship in the last 2 years). Fines up to **$10M CAD/violation (orgs), $1M CAD (individuals)**. ([moderninbound compliance](https://moderninbound.com/blog/cold-email-compliance-guide))
- **2026 trend:** regulators are actively cracking down on unsolicited commercial email and **AI-generated outreach is accelerating enforcement / creating new exposure**. Suppression, consent records, and jurisdiction handling must be first-class, not bolted on.

**Mandatory-NOW checklist to reach the inbox:** ① SPF + DKIM (aligned) on every sending domain · ② DMARC published (min p=none, RUA) · ③ RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe on marketing mail, honored ≤2 days · ④ complaint rate <0.3% (target <0.1%) monitored via Postmaster · ⑤ dedicated cold domain + subdomain, warmed · ⑥ verified list (bounce <3%) · ⑦ physical address + honest identification + working opt-out (CAN-SPAM) · ⑧ documented lawful basis per recipient jurisdiction (GDPR/CASL).

# Cold Email Phase 3 — Build Spec

Builds on the Phase 1/2 skeleton (businesses, contacts, lists, brands/sending-identities, suppression, one-click unsubscribe, gated send worker with warmup-ramp + daily caps, open/click tracking). Phase 3 = **warming, real analytics, and multi-domain/inbox rotation with health-based auto-pause**, plus baked-in compliance.

## A. Data model additions (Prisma)

**Domains & inboxes (the rotation substrate)**
- `SendingDomain` — `id, businessId, brandId, domain, subdomain, isPrimary(false), status(pending|warming|active|paused|burned), spfVerified, dkimVerified, dmarcPolicy(none|quarantine|reject), dmarcVerified, trackingDomain, trackingDomainVerified, addedAt, warmupStartedAt`.
- `Inbox` — `id, sendingDomainId, email, provider(gmail|m365|smtp|postal|kumo), imapConfig/smtpConfig(encrypted), status(warming|active|paused|burned), dailyCap, currentRampCap, warmupDay, lastSendAt, sendWindowStart/End, minGapSeconds(90–120), reputationScore(0–100)`.
- `InboxAuth` — SPF/DKIM/DMARC/tracking check results per domain with `lastCheckedAt` (re-verify on a schedule; DNS drifts).

**Warmup schedule & state (per inbox)**
- `WarmupPlan` — `inboxId, strategy(conservative|standard|aggressive|adaptive), startCap, targetCap, rampDays, dailyIncrement, mode(pool|real-seed|hybrid)`.
- `WarmupState` — `inboxId, day, plannedToday, sentToday, warmupRepliesToday, spamRescuesToday, healthScore, pausedReason`.
- `WarmupActivity` — event log of pool interactions (sent/opened/replied/marked-important/rescued-from-spam) for auditability and the honesty argument (we can show *what kind* of warmup ran).

**Deliverability events (the analytics spine)**
- `DeliverabilityEvent` — append-only: `id, inboxId, sendingDomainId, campaignId, contactId, messageId, type(sent|delivered|deferred|hard_bounce|soft_bounce|open|click|reply|positive_reply|complaint|unsubscribe|placement_test), subtype(bounce reason code, etc.), provider, occurredAt, raw`. Everything else rolls up from this table. Store SMTP/DSN codes so hard vs soft is derived, not guessed.
- `PlacementTest` — `id, sendingDomainId, provider(glockapps|mailreach|manual_seed), inbox%, spam%, promotions%, missing%, runAt` (seed-list results; the only trustworthy "in the inbox?" signal).

**Analytics rollups (precomputed for dashboards)**
- `MetricsDaily` — grain: `(date, scope=campaign|inbox|domain|business, scopeId)` with `sent, delivered, hardBounce, softBounce, opens(flagged unreliable), uniqueClicks, replies, positiveReplies, complaints, unsubscribes` + derived `deliveryRate, bounceRate, complaintRate, unsubRate, clickRate, replyRate, inboxPlacementRate(from latest PlacementTest)`. Roll up nightly + on-demand.
- `HealthSnapshot` — `(date, scope, scopeId, healthScore, status, triggeredRules[])` feeding auto-pause.

**Compliance**
- `ConsentRecord` — `contactId, lawfulBasis(legitimate_interest|consent|existing_relationship), jurisdiction, source, assessmentRef, capturedAt`.
- Extend `Suppression` with `reason(hard_bounce|complaint|unsubscribe|manual|global)` and enforce **global cross-campaign** suppression (already present — keep it authoritative).

## B. Warming UI

- **Per-inbox warmup dashboard:** ramp curve (planned vs actual daily volume), current day / target, health score, and a plain-language status ("Warming — day 9 of 21, on track").
- **Strategy picker:** conservative / standard / adaptive, with mode = *pool* / *real-seed* / *hybrid*. **Default to hybrid/real-seed and surface a warning** that synthetic-pool warmup can be detected and may hurt in 2026 (cite the debate) — don't present artificial warmup as risk-free.
- **Warmup activity feed** (opens/replies/spam-rescues) so the customer sees it's working and *what kind* of signals ran.
- **"Ready to send" gate:** block campaign sends from an inbox until warmup day ≥ threshold AND auth (SPF/DKIM/DMARC/tracking) all green — reuse the existing gated send worker.

## C. Analytics dashboards

- **Campaign view:** delivery, bounce (hard/soft split), reply + **positive-reply** (hero metric), click, complaint, unsubscribe, inbox-placement. Time series + funnel.
- **Open rate: show it, but flag it.** Render behind an "⚠ inflated by Apple MPP / scanners — not a reliable signal" tooltip, visually de-emphasized, never the headline and never an optimization target. This honesty is a differentiator vs tools that still lead with opens.
- **Deliverability/health view (per inbox & per domain):** reputation score, rolling bounce%, complaint%, unsub%, latest placement-test result, and burn-risk status with the exact thresholds (§4). Color: green <2% bounce/<0.05% complaint, amber to 5%/0.08%, red beyond.
- **Placement testing:** trigger/seed-test integration (GlockApps/MailReach API or an internal seed list) and chart inbox-vs-spam-vs-promotions over time.
- **Roll-ups** at business level for the agency/multi-client case.

## D. Multi-domain / multi-inbox management + rotation + auto-pause

- **Pool manager:** register domains → subdomains → inboxes; run and cache SPF/DKIM/DMARC/tracking verification; show a readiness matrix.
- **Rotation engine** in the send worker: distribute a campaign's daily sends round-robin across *eligible* inboxes (status=active, under `currentRampCap`, warmup complete, auth green), spacing sends `minGapSeconds` (90–120s) inside each inbox's send window; respect per-inbox and per-domain caps (20–40/inbox, ~100–250/domain). Persist last-used to avoid clustering.
- **Auto-pause on bad metrics (the safety system):** evaluate `HealthSnapshot` rules continuously —
  - bounce ≥1.8%/inbox/day → **pause inbox**; sustained >2% over multiple days → **pause domain**; >5% → **hard stop + require re-verification**.
  - complaint >0.08%/domain → **pause domain + flag targeting**.
  - On pause: stop new sends, keep the inbox warming, notify, and require manual/verified re-activation. Never silently keep burning a domain.
- **Deliverability inbox rescue:** on soft-bounce spikes, back off volume automatically (adaptive ramp down), don't just hard-pause.

## E. Compliance guardrails to bake in

- **Auth-or-no-send:** worker refuses to send from any domain lacking passing SPF+DKIM+DMARC (min p=none). This is now table stakes (§5).
- **RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe** on every message (`List-Unsubscribe` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post`), processed automatically ≤2 days → global suppression. (Extend Phase 1/2's unsubscribe.)
- **CAN-SPAM fields enforced** at template level: honest From/subject, physical postal address, working opt-out — block send if missing.
- **Consent/lawful-basis per contact & jurisdiction:** require a `ConsentRecord` (LIA for GDPR legitimate interest; existing-relationship for CASL); warn/block on EU/CA contacts without a basis. Flag France/CNIL Aug-2026 B2C explicit-opt-in.
- **Complaint-rate circuit breaker** wired to Postmaster/FBL data feeding the same auto-pause.
- **Global cross-campaign suppression** authoritative; never re-mail hard-bounces or complainers.
- **Verify-before-send:** integrate list verification (ZeroBounce/NeverBounce/Bouncer) as a pre-send step; block campaigns whose projected bounce (from verification) exceeds ~3%.

**Summary (<200 words)**

Cold email in 2026 is gated by authentication, not content. Google/Yahoo (Feb 2024) and Microsoft (May 2025) now *reject* bulk mail (5k+/day to consumers) that lacks aligned SPF+DKIM+DMARC, RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe, and a spam-complaint rate under 0.3% (target <0.1%) — Gmail escalated to permanent 550 rejections in Nov 2025. Build to that strict floor regardless of volume. There's no mature self-hostable OSS warmup *network* (the vetted-mailbox pool is the SaaS moat); Postal/KumoMTA are the best OSS references for the sending/events layer, and Warmbly is the closest OSS cold-email clone but its pool still runs in their cloud. Legit warmup now favors real replies/spam-rescue over synthetic pool traffic — artificial warmup is increasingly detectable and can hurt. Scale via 3–5 domains × 4–6 inboxes, 20–40 sends/inbox/day, on isolated subdomains with custom tracking domains.
